incidents.vector: A custom toolset called Cereal was embedded inside Microsoft Exchange services to intercept and exfiltrate email traffic, using the compromised servers themselves as command-and-control infrastructure.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole government email correspondence, including messages exchanged with NATO and EU officials in Romania; the Kazakhstan intrusion targeted a government email server amid scrutiny of Russian exiles.

incidents.victim: Organizations with internet-exposed SonicWall, Palo Alto Networks and Fortinet VPN appliances
incidents.vector: A group tracked as TAG-218 compromised internet-facing VPN appliances, then deployed a newly identified ESXi post-exploitation framework called GhostFrame to gain root-level hypervisor access, harvest credentials, and pivot across virtual machines.
incidents.impact: At least four victim organizations in the US and Europe were subsequently listed on the Settra ransomware leak site.

incidents.vector: Ransomware gang BYOD gained access to campus IT systems and claims to have stolen more than a million Social Security numbers.
incidents.impact: The university shut down campus WiFi and devices and took several digital services offline while it continues to contain and investigate the incident.

incidents.victim: EU politicians and law enforcement officials
incidents.vector: Pro-Kremlin hacktivist group NoName057(16) solicited personal information on adversaries through a dark web portal and published it as a dox.
incidents.impact: Personal information of 18 senior EU and law enforcement officials, including Italy's foreign minister and Europol's cybercrime chief, plus three journalists, was published online, raising physical safety concerns.

incidents.vector: Hackers gained unauthorized access to company files between January 18 and February 8, 2026.
incidents.impact: Social Security numbers, ID numbers, medical and health insurance information, and financial data were stolen; the company has notified over 86,800 people in Texas and Vermont, though class-action filings allege more than 1.3 million victims.

incidents.vector: Unspecified; the company has not disclosed the attack method.
incidents.impact: Patient names, email addresses, ID and passport numbers, dates of birth, emergency contacts and bank account details were stolen from Singapore's leading telemedicine provider.

incidents.vector: New ransomware group WhiteArmor claims to have breached Maersk's logistics platform.
incidents.impact: The group claims to have stolen 10GB of data, including driver records and delivery receipts, and is demanding a $5 million ransom; Maersk has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Hackers are taking over master user accounts tied to Chinese eSIMs used to register Li Auto connected-car accounts.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed owners have been locked out of their vehicles and extorted to regain control; the true number of affected cars is believed to be higher.

incidents.vector: A threat actor claims to have breached the Austrian jewelry company's systems.
incidents.impact: The actor claims to have stolen personal data of nearly 100,000 customers; Swarovski has not confirmed the incident.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached the MyTUM student and employee portal and stole stored passwords, including administrator accounts.
incidents.impact: The university took the portal offline and is forcing all users to reset their passwords.

incidents.vector: A hacker leaked data gathered from dozens of French sports federations, including swimming, handball, basketball, rugby, tennis and football bodies, some originating from older breaches.
incidents.impact: Member and organizational data from the federations was published online.

incidents.victim: Mittwald CM Service and 56 customer hosting projects
incidents.vector: Attackers allegedly using AI tools exploited a flaw in Mittwald's Model Context Protocol server, which lets customers connect AI assistants to its mStudio hosting platform, going undetected for eight days.
incidents.impact: 56 customer hosting projects were compromised; the company found no further attacker activity after forensic review and is publishing a full incident report.

incidents.vector: North Korean operatives, tracked by the FBI as TraderTraitor, stole tokens across 11 different cryptocurrencies from the exchange.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.3 billion was stolen, the largest cryptocurrency theft on record; about $2.8 billion in stablecoins was later frozen, leaving about $3.25 billion unrecoverable.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached a network used to process Gnosis-branded cryptocurrency payment cards.
incidents.impact: Cardholder information was stolen; the company enabled mandatory 3D Secure verification for all Gnosis card owners ahead of the network's planned retirement.

incidents.vector: Attackers gained unauthorized access to internet-exposed refrigeration controllers, likely via vulnerable software or default credentials, and forced them into defrost mode.
incidents.impact: A second wave hit 100-115 retail locations across 10+ European countries; some units reached 50°C and caused fires, and French medical facility refrigeration was also affected, though no blood products were reportedly spoiled.

incidents.victim: Organizations with internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces
incidents.vector: Attackers chained the PHP2Shell remote code execution vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619) with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaw to gain root access to internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Unit 42 confirmed active exploitation against roughly 0.02% of its customer base with internet-facing management interfaces; affected customers were individually notified and patched systems are protected.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite, defense, aerospace and policy research organizations using Cisco SD-WAN
incidents.vector: Threat actor UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controller, to deploy a custom malware framework that intercepts decrypted control-plane traffic and keying material.
incidents.impact: Attackers gained long-term persistent access to compromised Cisco SD-WAN controllers to collect sensitive network keying material; Talos assesses the operating infrastructure overlaps with a known China-linked covert access network.

incidents.vector: A financially motivated group breached Fireworks' systems in early October, then used a compromised third-party cloud provider to reach Fireworks' development machines and run an unauthorized workload.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole billing information, secrets, and AI-related datasets from a limited number of customer accounts; downstream customer Notion disconnected from Fireworks and disabled a dependent feature.

incidents.vector: Hackers breached government networks and began extracting data before IT staff detected the intrusion.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole personal data on roughly a third of Moldova's population; officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: 40+ port authorities, maritime and global shipping companies
incidents.vector: Ransomware group n0n compromised maritime IT services provider CyberLogitec and pivoted from its network into dozens of downstream shipping company customers.
incidents.impact: All victims were listed on n0n's dark web leak site, and the group's payment deadline for the affected companies has already expired.

incidents.victim: University of New Mexico Health Sciences Center
incidents.vector: Ransomware gang BYOD, first observed September 29, breached the health sciences center's systems.
incidents.impact: The attack disrupted patient care and caused system outages at one of the state's only top-tier hospitals, forcing it to turn away ambulances.
